questions.question: What is the minimum depth of fast-moving floodwater capable of floating most passenger vehicles?
options: 10 cm (4 inches)
30 cm (12 inches)
100 cm (3.3 feet)
150 cm (5 feet)
questions.explanation: Just 30 cm (12 inches) of moving water exerts enough lateral buoyancy to float and destabilize most passenger cars, leading to loss of steering control.

questions.question: If floodwater begins entering your ground-floor living room, what is the safest electrical safety action?
options: Wade to the main circuit breaker to switch it off immediately.
Do NOT touch any switches or breakers; evacuate immediately to an upper floor.
Unplug refrigerator and TV with wet hands.
Wait in the room until the water level reaches your knees.
questions.explanation: NDMA protocol strictly advises: Never touch electrical switches, meters, or appliances if water is present or if your feet/hands are wet. Move to upper floors immediately.

questions.question: Which deadly water-borne bacterial infection is common in Kerala following flood inundation, transmitted through contaminated animal urine?
options: Malaria
Leptospirosis (Rat Fever / എലിപ്പനി)
Dengue
Chikungunya
questions.explanation: Leptospirosis is caused by Leptospira bacteria entering through cuts or mucous membranes from floodwaters contaminated by rodent urine. Prophylactic Doxycycline is recommended by health authorities.

questions.question: Under the 'Turn Around, Don't Drown' national protocol, what should you do if encountering a flooded road while driving?
options: Accelerate fast to cross before the engine floods.
Follow closely behind a heavy commercial truck.
Turn around and seek an alternate elevated route.
Get out and push the car across.
questions.explanation: Nearly half of all flood fatalities occur in trapped vehicles. Roads and bridges can collapse beneath water surfaces unseen. Turn around immediately.

questions.question: What is the single nationwide Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) number across India?
questions.explanation: 112 is India's unified all-in-one emergency helpline operational for Police, Fire, Ambulance, and Disaster Search & Rescue.

questions.question: What is the internationally recognized safety action during an earthquake tremor?
options: Stand upright and scream for help
Run towards the nearest exit door immediately
Drop, Cover, and Hold On
Run onto the building balcony
questions.explanation: NDMA strongly emphasizes 'Drop, Cover, and Hold On' beneath sturdy desks or tables to protect your head and vitals from falling masonry and shattered glass.

questions.question: Why should you NEVER use an elevator to evacuate after an earthquake?
options: Elevators move too slowly during emergencies.
Shafts and electrical systems can warp or lose power, trapping occupants between floors.
Elevator buttons will give an electrical shock.
Building codes require elevator use for pets only.
questions.explanation: Tremors twist elevator guide rails and interrupt electrical grids, making elevators severe death traps. Always use designated fire-exit stairs.

questions.question: If you suspect a gas leak inside your house following an earthquake, what should you do?
options: Switch on ceiling lights to inspect the gas pipe.
Light a matchstick to check if gas is burning.
Turn off the cylinder regulator if safe, open windows for ventilation, and do NOT touch electrical switches.
Pour water onto the stove burners.
questions.explanation: Electrical switches produce minute electrical arcs that instantly ignite leaking gas. Open windows, shut main valves, evacuate, and use battery torches.

questions.question: If you are trapped beneath debris after an earthquake collapse, what is the best signaling technique?
options: Shout continuously without stopping.
Tap rhythmically on metal pipes, beams, or use a whistle.
Ignite a lighter to illuminate rescuers.
Try to break concrete slabs with your bare hands.
questions.explanation: Tapping on pipes or using a whistle travels through rubble over long distances and saves oxygen and vital stamina. Shouting should be reserved only when hearing rescuers nearby.

questions.question: If an intense earthquake occurs while you are on a coastal beach, what immediate hazard should you anticipate?
options: Cyclone
Tsunami waves
Landslide
Hailstorm
questions.explanation: Undersea or coastal earthquakes frequently trigger tsunami waves. Move immediately to high ground at least 2 km inland or 30 meters above sea level.

questions.question: Which of the following is an early physical indicator of slope instability preceding a landslide?
options: Sudden cooling of outdoor ambient temperature
Widening ground tension cracks and tilting trees or utility poles
Formation of dense fog around treetops
Sudden increase in bird chirping
questions.explanation: Ground shear stress reveals itself through progressive surface cracks, buckling retaining walls, and tilting vertical poles and trees before total slope failure.

questions.question: If caught in the path of a rapidly descending mudslide or debris flow, which direction should you flee?
options: Downslope along the natural stream valley channel
Perpendicular (sideways) towards stable, elevated ground
Climb up into a tall tree in the flow path
Lie flat in the ditch
questions.explanation: Debris flows travel with immense momentum down valley channels. Running sideways (perpendicular) escapes the chute into stable topography.

questions.question: Which districts in Kerala are classified by KSDMA and GSI as highly susceptible to catastrophic landslides during intense monsoon deluges?
options: Alappuzha and Kollam coastal plains
Wayanad, Idukki, and hilly taluks of Pathanamthitta / Malappuram
Kochi urban corporation
Kozhikode beach promenade
questions.explanation: Wayanad, Idukki, and the high-ranges of the Western Ghats have steep slopes and high rainfall susceptibility, as witnessed in Meppadi (Wayanad) and Pettimudi (Idukki).

questions.question: What should you do if escape from an active landslide is physically impossible?
options: Run into a small basement.
Curl tightly into a ball, pull knees to chest, and shield your head with your hands/helmet.
Jump into the nearest moving stream.
Stand against a glass window to signal out.
questions.explanation: NDMA advises: If escape is blocked, curl into a tight fetal ball and shield your head with cushions or sturdy objects to minimize blunt-force trauma to vital organs.

questions.question: After a landslide halts, why is it dangerous to immediately enter the debris zone to salvage property?
options: Government fines are imposed immediately.
Secondary slides, hanging boulders, and flash floods from blocked streams frequently follow.
The ground turns into quicksand within seconds.
Helicopters will blow dust into the house.
questions.explanation: Debris dams can burst, and unstabilized head scarps often experience secondary collapses. Wait until geotechnical and disaster teams declare the site safe.
